title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: The Transformer organized sequence modeling around attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions in its proposed architecture. The paper evaluated the design on machine translation.
contribution: A sequence architecture with self-attention and parallelizable training, evaluated against translation baselines.
limit: Translation results do not establish every later capability associated with Transformer-based models.
question: When we add more context, which information actually changes an answer?

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
summary: RAG combined a parametric sequence-to-sequence model with a non-parametric index of Wikipedia passages accessed through dense retrieval. Its evaluations included knowledge-intensive tasks.
contribution: A model that combines retrieved documents with generation instead of relying only on information encoded in parameters.
limit: Retrieval does not guarantee that every generated claim follows from a retrieved passage.
question: Can a reader trace each important claim back to evidence that actually supports it?

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
summary: FlashAttention used tiling to reduce reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM while computing exact attention. The paper reported gains for its tested configurations.
contribution: Attention computation organized around data movement and the GPU memory hierarchy.
limit: Reported speedups depend on the hardware, sequence length, implementation, and comparison baseline.
question: Which cost dominates this workload: arithmetic, memory traffic, or the rest of the system?

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
summary: PagedAttention addressed KV-cache memory fragmentation and sharing during language-model serving. The paper introduced the vLLM serving system and evaluated throughput under several workloads.
contribution: Block-based KV-cache management that separates logical token positions from physical memory allocation.
limit: Better allocation does not eliminate the cache memory required to store active sequences.
question: How much usable context remains when many people generate at the same time?

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
summary: Self-RAG trained a model to use special reflection tokens for on-demand retrieval and critiques of generated output. The authors evaluated factuality, generation quality, and citation behavior.
contribution: Retrieval and critique decisions integrated into a trained generation process.
limit: A model’s own critique remains a fallible signal, rather than independent verification of every claim.
question: Who checks the checker when an answer and its critique share the same blind spot?

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
summary: AgentDojo introduced an extensible environment for evaluating tool-using agents, prompt-injection attacks, and defenses. Its tasks place agents in contact with untrusted data while they carry out user requests.
contribution: A setting for measuring both task utility and security behavior in agent workflows.
limit: Performance on a benchmark is evidence about tested cases, not proof that a deployed agent is secure.
question: Where does data stop being data and start being treated as authority?

title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
summary: GR00T N1 described a robot foundation model combining a vision-language component with diffusion-based action generation. Training incorporated real robot data, human video, and synthetic data, with evaluation in simulation and on a humanoid platform.
contribution: A dual-system architecture and heterogeneous data strategy for humanoid robot learning.
limit: The reported platforms and tasks do not imply compatibility with every robot, sensor, or action space.
question: What data contract makes an action meaningful on a different body?

title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
summary: π0.5 explored co-training on heterogeneous tasks and data, including multiple robot embodiments and high-level semantic prediction. The paper reported household-task experiments in homes outside the robot training environments.
contribution: A co-training approach connecting semantic knowledge and robot action learning for generalization.
limit: Reported generalization experiments do not guarantee reliable operation under every household condition.
question: Which changes in environment, object, or embodiment would break this policy first?
